status: accepted
decision: Owner execution commission of 2026-10-27; preserve existing product obligations and compare candidates without preselecting a winner.

# Bridge delivery comparison

## Purpose

Help the person sending a nudge reach the correct agent quickly and recover work after interruption, with measured evidence for any bridge replacement.

The comparison preserves [product behavior](../PRODUCT.md) and the
[repository test obligations](../../CONTRIBUTING.md). Rust is experimental until
it meets the same independently expected behavior as JavaScript and demonstrates
an operational benefit. There is no installation or release decision here.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Compare preserved delivery behavior independently
ID: bridge-delivery-reference

Both candidates preserve the following observable obligations through the same external expectations.

| ID | Obligation |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | Confirmed acceptance survives bridge-process restart on a functioning filesystem. |
| BR-02 | A stable submission identity has one stored effect through the supported retry horizon. |
| BR-03 | Conflicting content under that identity is explicitly refused without replacing original work. |
| BR-04 | Browser-accepted work remains recoverable in durable acceptance order within one installation. |
| BR-05 | Preserve opt-in, host routing and immutable committed ownership. |
| BR-06 | Distinguish reachable bridge, fresh watcher and actual push capability truthfully. |
| BR-07 | Eligible participants automatically recover transient transport/process interruptions using original identities. |
| BR-08 | Malformed and slow peers cannot crash or indefinitely starve healthy clients. |
| BR-09 | Selection and evidence remain bound to their browser, tab, document, route and mark generation. |
| BR-10 | Preserve wire/file compatibility and direct CLI/hook/watcher readers; refuse unsafe changes before mutation. |
| BR-11 | Measure named boundaries with independent expectations and every attempt retained. |
| BR-12 | Start/stop/upgrade affect only positively identified owned instances. |

The [reference examples](../../test/fixtures/bridge-comparison/reference-cases.json)
are reviewed independent event timelines. They are not expected-result functions
imported from either candidate. RC01–RC12 remain bounded by their explicit policy
dependencies. In particular, a stored effect is distinct from a watcher wake and
from an actual agent input. Exact-once model execution is not promised.

#### Scenario: Reject plausible false success
- GIVEN a pre-registered input and expected owner
- WHEN a candidate drops it, stores it twice or stamps a foreign owner
- THEN the independent ledger rejects that candidate for the intended assertion.

## Experiment boundaries

The [frozen experiment policy](../../test/fixtures/bridge-comparison/policy.json)
is an engineering comparison policy, not a new product service-level promise.
Its hash must be retained before Rust qualification. Process-crash recovery is
the common durability class; no fsync/power-loss claim follows from a successful
rename. OS/power-loss durability remains outside this experiment.

Owner selection at server acceptance and later ownership immutability retain
current behavior. Pre-commit ownership switches and ambiguous offline selection
remain unqualified rather than acquiring a new rule through these tests. Corrupt
original files must be preserved; complete recovery from irrecoverable bytes is
not claimed. The initial compatibility subject is the reviewed handoff snapshot;
a broader historical/platform support matrix is not implied.

T0 is the harness timestamp immediately before a ready Send button receives real
pointer input. Geometry/actionability preparation is outside T0; dispatch and
watcher pipe observation costs remain inside. TW is exact watcher stdout matched
to browser request identity and independent expected payload/owner. TA observes
HTTP response headers; UI disappearance is only an upper bound for queue UI
acknowledgement, not an instrumented storage-acknowledgement timestamp TQ.
TS requires supported input-boundary evidence from an actual opted-in host. A
synthetic watcher and an eventual model answer cannot establish TS. Pull waiting
and model scheduling must remain separate from transport latency.

All tests use private stores, side ports, profiles and synthetic identities. Test
extension native autostart is disabled before loading. Google Chrome uses an
isolated debugging pipe and `Extensions.loadUnpacked`; this is an automated
unpacked lane, not native lifecycle or distribution acceptance. Compare the same
extension/watcher bytes, data, deadlines and durability class. Keep all failed
setup attempts, timeouts and negative controls. Never run long qualification on
a candidate failing essential conformance.

# Run the isolated bridge comparison

The [canonical requirements](specs/bridge-delivery.md) and
[frozen policy](../test/fixtures/bridge-comparison/policy.json) define the experiment.
The Rust executable is experimental and refuses the default bridge port. The
JavaScript bridge remains the installed default. None of these commands installs,
publishes, merges or changes an ordinary browser/agent profile.

From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix bridge
npm ci --prefix test
cargo test --locked --manifest-path bridge-rust/Cargo.toml
cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path bridge-rust/Cargo.toml
npm run test:ci --prefix test
node test/bridge-mutants.mjs
node test/bridge-conformance.mjs
node test/bridge-image-conformance.mjs
node test/bridge-retention.mjs
```

Use the same commands/expectations with a candidate argument array:

```sh
export NUDGE_CANDIDATE='["./bridge-rust/target/release/nudge-bridge-experiment"]'
node test/bridge-conformance.mjs
node test/bridge-image-conformance.mjs
node test/bridge-retention.mjs
node test/browser-protocol.mjs
node test/bridge-boundary.mjs
node test/bridge-realtime.mjs
unset NUDGE_CANDIDATE
node test/bridge-rollback.mjs
node test/bridge-harness-interrupt.mjs
```

Only startup is parameterized in the three existing protocol suites; their
assertions remain unchanged. They use isolated resources and must run serially.
The existing [portable/browser runners](../CONTRIBUTING.md#tests) remain required.
Suite A runs first in the browser runner. Chromium, Chrome for Testing and actual
Google Chrome are separate lanes. Google Chrome is loaded through the documented
[DevTools extension API](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Extensions/#method-loadUnpacked)
in a throwaway profile, with native autostart disabled before the worker loads.

```sh
node test/chrome-delivery.mjs --browser chrome --samples 30
node test/chrome-delivery.mjs --browser chromium --headless --samples 10
node test/bridge-compare.mjs --blocks 3 --samples 20
node test/bridge-resources.mjs
```

Paired runs alternate candidate order from a fixed seed, use the same extension,
watcher and inputs, and retain every attempted input, failure and timeout. The
paired command performs essential external checks before timing. Results are
**diagnostic and inconclusive for adoption**; `--qualify` refuses while complete
catalog/coverage/mutation, native/host/OS and soak prerequisites are missing.
Bridge-only RSS samples and direct HTTP timing do not establish whole-system cost
or Chrome-to-agent speed. Pull waiting and model scheduling remain separate.

Crash barriers use dedicated instrumented builds, never timing builds:

```sh
node test/bridge-commit-faults.mjs
cargo build --locked --release --features fault-hooks --manifest-path bridge-rust/Cargo.toml
NUDGE_CANDIDATE='["./bridge-rust/target/release/nudge-bridge-experiment"]' node test/bridge-commit-faults.mjs
cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path bridge-rust/Cargo.toml
```

The final command restores the production-feature build. File writes/rename and
SIGKILL establish process-crash evidence on a functioning OS, not power-loss
safety. Deterministic pre-write/post-write/pre-rename/post-rename tests do not yet
cover all partial writes, withdrawal/evidence races, sync/ENOSPC simulations or
production random-kill schedules.

Evidence is retained under `artifacts/bridge-comparison/` and the existing
`artifacts/safari/` runner directories. Source manifests include hashes of tracked
and relevant untracked files; candidate executable bytes are bound separately in
Chrome/retention reports. Earlier failed setup runs and red regressions remain.
The [catalog](../test/fixtures/bridge-comparison/catalog.json) maps all 115 IDs to
specific assertions or explicit missing drivers/platform/host prerequisites;
a mapped or partially exercised case is never automatically passed.

JS0 is the reviewed handoff snapshot. JS1 adds the shared retired-socket callback
fix in extension 0.35.2; both candidates use JS1 extension bytes for paired runs.
No Node bridge, queue deadline, storage durability or watcher change is credited
to Rust. Rust still leaves the CLI/hook/watcher dependent on Node.

# Contributing to Nudge

Thanks for helping. This page tells you how the repository works so that a
pull request lands without surprises.

If you are a coding agent working **in this checkout**, start at
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). If you only want to *use* Nudge on another project,
stop here and follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) — invoke `/groundworks-nudge`
there, not here.

Read [docs/VISION.md](docs/VISION.md) first: it lists the non-goals (no
annotation tool, no cloud, no framework adapters), and a PR that crosses one
of them will not be merged however good the code is.

## Dev setup

```sh
git clone https://github.com/gstangl/nudge-extension.git
cd nudge-extension
(cd bridge && npm ci)             # locked runtime dependency: ws
(cd test && npm ci)               # locked vitest + playwright
(cd test && npx playwright install chromium)   # browser for the e2e suites
```

For actual project use, follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for Chrome or the
[temporary Safari guide](docs/SAFARI.md). Browser tests below stage isolated
resources and do not require installing into your everyday browser. The shared
extension is plain JavaScript without a bundler; Safari resources are staged
deterministically. The bridge and CLI are plain ES modules run by Node 22+.

**Chrome dev auto-reload.** While a bridge runs, it watches `extension/`. On any
change it tells Chrome's unpacked extension to reload itself and refreshes the
localhost tabs. Safari's release-configured temporary resources disable this;
[restage and reload them](docs/SAFARI.md#updates-and-removal) explicitly. (Under
Playwright's `--load-extension` the reload kills the extension instead, so
`test/autoreload-check.mjs` is a manual check.)

**Bridge changes.** Follow the identity-checked
[restart instructions](INSTALL.md#updating). Never stop an unknown listener or
the live shared bridge to run tests; test bridges use separate ports and stores.

## Tests

Three layers. Run the first before every push; run the relevant Playwright
suites when you touch the extension or the bridge.

1. **Fast gate, required in CI**
   ```sh
   cd test && npm run test:ci
   ```
   Vitest units for `store.mjs` and `runtime.mjs`, the runtime-neutral
   integration (real bridge, real watcher, CLI, hook), and the idempotent
   installer check. Takes a few seconds, needs no browser.

2. **Playwright suites**, each a standalone script with its own bridge on a
   side port and a throwaway store. The contract, the legs and the last
   results are in [test/protocols.md](test/protocols.md). The ones every
   contributor can run are listed below. Prefer the serial isolated runners:

   ```sh
   node test/run-portable-regression.mjs
   node test/run-browser-regression.mjs --headless
   node test/browser-parity.mjs --chromium --headless
   node test/browser-coexistence.mjs --chromium-only --headless
   ```

   Do not run them concurrently. For an individual browser suite, stage a
   native-disabled test package **before** loading its worker. Setting only
   `nudgePort` after startup is too late to prevent native autostart:

   ```sh
   node scripts/package-safari.mjs --mode test --use-storage-port --out artifacts/safari/manual-test-extension
   export NUDGE_EXT="$PWD/artifacts/safari/manual-test-extension"
   export NUDGE_NO_RELOAD=1
   ```

   This package is only for tests, never the Safari project installation.
   Individual suites (from the repository root, with that test environment):

   ```sh
   node test/e2e.mjs               # Suite A: the core end-to-end run
   node test/bridge-brutal.mjs     # Suite D: adversarial bridge (about 90 s)
   node test/bridge-hardening.mjs
   node test/fixture-gauntlet.mjs  # Suite F: third-party UIs (needs python3)
   node test/origin-routing.mjs    # Suite K
   node test/toolbar-ux.mjs        # Suite L
   node test/page-inertness.mjs    # Suite M
   node test/amend.mjs             # Suite N
   node test/escape-clear.mjs      # Suite O
   node test/multi-select.mjs      # Suite P
   node test/reload-resilience.mjs # Suite Q
   node test/wake-mode.mjs         # Suite W
   node test/cancel.mjs            # Suite X
   node test/capture-stall.mjs     # Suite Y
   node test/off-means-off.mjs     # Suite Z
   node test/hook-optin.mjs        # Suite G
   node test/provenance.mjs        # Suite H
   node test/battletest.mjs        # Suite I (needs python3)
   ```
   Suites E, B and J (`real-apps.mjs`, `live-drill.mjs`, `cross-app.mjs`)
   drive the maintainers' private apps and are not runnable from this
   repository alone.

3. **Manual drills** listed in `test/protocols.md` under Suite C, each tied to
   a trigger ("run after X changed").

Standing rules: tests never touch port 4700 or the live store; every suite
uses its own side port. If an interrupted run leaves a bridge or watcher
behind, kill it by its side port, never by process name (a `watch-nudges`
process is usually somebody's real armed session). Verify the listener belongs
to the exact test before stopping it; an occupied side port may be unrelated.

External tools the test layer needs: Node 22+, Playwright's Chromium
(`npx playwright install chromium`), and `python3` for the two suites that
serve static fixtures with `http.server`. The product itself needs none of
these.

Suite D's LAN-bind check also requires a non-loopback IPv4 interface. Without
one it reports a blocked check and exits nonzero; it cannot prove LAN isolation
on an offline loopback-only machine. Watcher fixtures use their own identities,
so tests do not require running inside a coding-agent session.

## Versioning and changelog

- The extension version in `extension/manifest.json` is the product version.
  The bridge has its own version in `bridge/bridge.mjs` (`VERSION`) and
  `bridge/package.json`.
- Bump on every behaviour change, and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry in the same
  change (Keep a Changelog format, newest first, `Added / Changed / Fixed /
  Removed / Security`). No silent releases.
- Write the entry for the reader who hits the behaviour, not for the author:
  what changed, why, and how it is proven (which suite leg).

## Code conventions

- **Plain ES modules, no bundler, no TypeScript, no framework** in the
  extension. This keeps "load unpacked" a one-click install and lets the bridge
  reload the extension without a build.
- **English everywhere**: code, comments, UI strings, agent-facing strings,
  docs, changelog. No personal names, machine paths or ids in the repository.
- Comments explain *why*, and bug lessons keep their date ("2026-07-29: a
  stalled capture used to hide the toolbar"). That history is how the next
  person avoids re-breaking things.
- The store schema (`~/.nudge/store.json`, the `inbox/*.md` mirrors) and the
  bridge HTTP/WS routes are contracts between three parts that update
  independently. Change them additively, and update `test/unit/store.test.mjs`
  and the affected suites in the same PR.
- Keep the opt-in fence: a session appears in the browser only after the user
  invoked the Skill in it. No code path may arm a watcher or inject Nudge
  context into a session that did not opt in.
- Vendored code (`extension/vendor/finder.js`) is replaced wholesale from the
  upstream dist build; keep the `window.__nudgeFinder` export line.

## Pull requests

1. Fork or branch, one topic per PR. Small is good.
2. Run `npm run test:ci` and the Playwright suites that cover what you touched.
   Name them in the PR description.
3. Bump the version and add the changelog entry.
4. If you changed a workflow decision (how the repo is organised, not what
   the product does), add a dated entry to `docs/DECISIONS.md`, newest first,
   with what was rejected and why.
5. Fill in the PR template. CI must be green.

Where to start: `test/scenarios.md` has a backlog of edge cases worth
automating, and Windows support for the native host installer is open. The
terminal, Zed and T3 Code are tested; reports from other agent surfaces still
help. Good first issues are labelled `good first issue` when they exist.

## Reporting bugs and security issues

Bugs: open an issue with the template. Security: see
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Please do not file vulnerabilities as public
issues.
